title: deployment-stage-compact-cards-accessibility-animation-guidance
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design guidance and QA checklist for a new compact 'deployment stage' card used in the Deployments / Rollouts area of the Console. This ticket captures micro-interaction specs (including a toastless confirmation pattern), keyboard & screen-reader behavior, reduced-motion fallbacks, edge-case layouts when many stages exist, and handoff artifacts for engineering and QA.
synthesis_summary: We decided to adopt a compact card variant that supports dense and glance modes, avoids transient toast messages (uses inline ephemeral banners instead), and prioritizes keyboard-first confirmation patterns. Motion reduced for users with prefers-reduced-motion. Accessibility flows and telemetry event names standardized. Stakeholders approved the visual direction pending a small color-contrast tweak in the neutral CTA state.
acceptance_criteria: Compact deployment-stage card implemented in both dense and normal density modes
Confirmation flow uses inline ephemeral banner (no toast) and is keyboard-accessible (Enter to confirm, Esc to cancel)
All animations respect prefers-reduced-motion and have a reduced-duration alternative
Screen-reader announces stage name, state, and primary action; focus lands on primary action after opening details
Visual contrast of CTAs meets AA contrast ratios (4.5:1) and validated with color-blindness simulations
Behavior when >8 stages: horizontal scroll with visible gradient masks + accessible pagination controls
qa_checklist: Verify key interactions with keyboard only (Tab order, Enter to confirm, Escape to close)
Test screen reader sequence in NVDA and VoiceOver for stage cards and ephemeral banner
Simulate high-stage-count page (12+ stages) to validate truncation, scroll and pagination controls
Confirm reduced-motion mode disables non-essential motion and still provides meaningful state change
Validate inline ephemeral banner dismisses after 6s and is focusable when active (aria-live polite)
Cross-browser visual QA (Chrome, Firefox, Safari macOS/iOS) at scale (50 cards) to catch layout regressions
Run color contrast checks and a11y audits (axe-core) and attach reports
